entries.summary: The ship's reactor and the most valuable thing aboard. It starts melting down the moment it is separated from its mounting.
actions: Watch its stability on the HUD once the meltdown starts
Use the Scanner's Systems Mode to see what it is connected to
dismantle: Before touching it, clear a wide, straight path from the reactor to the Barge.
Strip the ship's power and coolant systems first - that leaves the reactor more stable when it goes.
A Class I reactor slides out of its coolant casing with a firm Grapple pull.
Move it straight into the {destination} before its stability runs out.
warnings: Separating it from its mounting starts a meltdown you cannot stop.
If stability reaches zero it explodes violently.
tips: On some ships the reactor controls sit behind a locked terminal; a Utility Key opens it.

entries.summary: A Class II reactor. Hugely valuable, but it starts melting down as soon as it is disconnected.
actions: Watch its stability on the HUD once the meltdown starts
Use the Scanner's Systems Mode to see what it is connected to
dismantle: Clear a wide path from the reactor to the Barge before anything else.
Release the reactor's connection to the thrusters.
Remove the coolant at the ship's ECU. Doing both of these steps gives you the slowest meltdown.
Strip the ship's power and coolant systems for extra stability.
Free the reactor and move it straight into the {destination} before its stability runs out.
warnings: Separating it from its mounting starts a meltdown you cannot stop.
If stability reaches zero it explodes violently.
tips: On some ships the reactor and thruster controls sit behind a locked terminal; a Utility Key opens it.

entries.summary: Reactor housing and mounting hardware. Valuable structure for the Processor - the reactor core itself goes to the Barge.
dismantle: Leave it in place until the reactor core is out and in the Barge.
Then cut it free with the {tools} and send it to the {destination}.
warnings: Cutting the housing while the core is still mounted can disconnect the reactor and start its meltdown.

entries.summary: Powers the ship. It stays live until every fuse connected to it has been pulled.
actions: Use the Scanner's Systems Mode to find its fuses
dismantle: Find every fuse. Red lights around the generator mean fuses are still connected.
Pull each fuse only while its indicator lights are all off.
When the last fuse is out the generator powers down safely.
Cut it free and send it to the {destination}.
warnings: Cutting or pulling it free while it is still live is dangerous.
tips: Every fuse you pull makes the remaining fuses cycle faster - stay ready.

entries.summary: One of the power generator's fuses. Its lights blink in a cycle; it is only safe to pull while they are all off.
actions: Pull the release lever while the lights are off
dismantle: Watch the indicator lights next to it.
The moment all of them are off, pull the release lever.
Collect the fuse by hand.
warnings: Pulling it while any light is on gives you an electric jolt.
tips: Every fuse you pull makes the remaining fuses cycle faster.

entries.summary: Indicator lights for a generator fuse. While any of them are lit, the fuse is still live.
dismantle: Leave them alone until their fuse has been pulled.
Then salvage them in the {destination}.

entries.summary: Holds ship fuel. Valuable intact, dangerous when damaged.
dismantle: Never cut into the tank itself.
Free it by cutting its mounts, connections or cut points.
Move it gently - hard impacts and fire can set it off.
Deliver it to the {destination}.
warnings: Cutting, burning or slamming it can ignite the fuel.
tips: Keep it away from fires and arcing electrics while you move it.

entries.summary: Carries fuel around the ship. A cut line sprays combustible fuel.
dismantle: Cut it at its ends or mounts rather than through the middle.
Make sure nothing nearby is burning or arcing first.
Send it to the {destination}.
warnings: Leaking fuel catches fire easily.

entries.summary: Fuel for your suit thrusters. Grab it to top up.
A damaged fuel pickup. It is no use to you any more - dispose of it in the Furnace.
Oxygen for your suit. Grab it to top up.
Unlocks restricted terminals - on some ships those control the reactor and thrusters.
Holds coolant. Worth salvaging intact.
dismantle: Don't cut into it.
Free it at its mounts and connections.
Deliver it to the {destination}.
warnings: A ruptured coolant container sprays freezing coolant. Frozen things turn brittle and can shatter.
tips: Coolant puts out fires and neutralizes radiation - a leak can occasionally work in your favour.

entries.summary: Carries coolant around the ship. Leaks if cut.
dismantle: Cut it at its ends or mounts and stay out of the spray.
Send it to the {destination}.
tips: Dismantling the ship's ECU stops a coolant leak that is getting out of hand.

entries.summary: Environmental Control Unit. Runs the ship's coolant, pressure and air filtering.
dismantle: Pull out its EC Unit modules (Cryo, Filter, Pressurization) - each one is salvage on its own.
Removing the Cryo module can flood connected systems with coolant, so stand clear of coolant lines.
Cut the ECU free and send it to the {destination}.
tips: Dismantling the ECU stops runaway coolant leaks.
Removing the coolant here before freeing a Class II reactor gives it a slower meltdown.

entries.summary: Control terminal for the Environmental Control Unit.
dismantle: Use any interactions you need first.
Cut it free and send it to the {destination}.

entries.summary: The ECU's coolant module.
dismantle: Stand clear of coolant pipes before you pull it.
Pull it free and send it to the {destination}.
warnings: Removing it can flood connected systems with coolant.

entries.summary: The ECU's pressurization module. Atmosphere Regulators depend on it.
dismantle: Depressurize rooms with their Atmosphere Regulators before you touch it.
Pull it free and send it to the {destination}.
warnings: If this module is damaged, Atmosphere Regulators stop working.

entries.summary: The ECU's air filter module.
dismantle: Pull it free and send it to the {destination}.

entries.summary: Controls a room's air pressure. Use it to vent the room safely before you cut into it.
actions: Use it to depressurize the room
dismantle: Use it to depressurize the room first.
Then cut it free and send it to the {destination}.
warnings: Some regulators are damaged and won't work. Then open the room from outside while standing clear of the breach.

entries.summary: A fuel-fed main thruster. Valuable, and explosive if you cut it wrong.
dismantle: Remove the Thruster Cap or access panel to expose the internal cut points.
Cut those cut points with the Stinger - never cut the thruster body.
Pull it free and send it to the {destination}.
warnings: Cutting into the thruster body can make it explode.

entries.summary: A cover over a thruster's internal cut points.
dismantle: Remove it to reach the cut points underneath.
Send it to the {destination}.

entries.summary: Quasar Thruster. Fragile and volatile, but it can be separated from its fuel source.
dismantle: Separate it from its fuel source first.
Handle it gently - it breaks easily.
Send it to the {destination}.
warnings: Volatile: don't cut it or knock it around.

entries.summary: Feeds fuel into a thruster.
dismantle: Treat it as a fuel part: make sure nothing nearby is burning or arcing.
Free it at its mounts with the {tools} and send it to the {destination}.

entries.summary: Thruster nozzle. It comes off by cutting through the external chassis that holds it.
dismantle: Cut it away through the surrounding external chassis.
Send it to the {destination}.

entries.summary: An engine nacelle mounted on the hull.
dismantle: Look for its connections inside the hull as well as outside.
Cut it loose at its cut points and send it to the {destination}.
tips: On some Mackerel ships the nacelles can only be disconnected from inside the hull.

entries.summary: Stores power. While it is intact, the ship's electrical systems can stay live.
dismantle: Remove it early - fewer systems stay powered once it is gone.
Pull it free gently and send it to the {destination}.
warnings: It can arc when removed, hit or damaged.

entries.summary: Distributes power through the ship.
dismantle: Check Systems Mode for what feeds it and remove those power sources first.
Cut it free and send it to the {destination}.
warnings: While the ship has power it can arc and briefly electrify nearby metal.

entries.summary: A ship terminal. Some have interactions - open doors, read logs or unlock systems.
dismantle: Use any interactions you need first; once it is cut free it stops working.
Cut it free at its mounts and send it to the {destination}.
tips: Locked terminals that control reactors and thrusters open with a Utility Key.

entries.summary: A powered door. It only opens while the ship has power.
dismantle: Open it while the ship still has power if you need to get through.
Check whether it seals a pressurized room before you cut it.
Cut it free and send it to the {destination}.

entries.summary: Part of the ship's airlock.
dismantle: Check whether the rooms behind it are still pressurized.
Depressurize them with their Atmosphere Regulator first.
Cut it free and send it to the {destination}.
warnings: Airlocks usually separate pressurized rooms from space.

entries.summary: Windows and canopies go to the Furnace.
dismantle: Depressurize the room behind it first.
Cut it free and send it to the {destination}.
warnings: Glass often seals a pressurized room - breaking it causes a decompression.

entries.summary: Nanocarbon. High-value structure that only enhanced cutting gear gets through.
dismantle: Check that it doesn't seal a pressurized room.
If your cutter's grade is too low, free it by cutting the parts around it.
Send it to the {destination}.

entries.summary: Hull plating. Its salvage destination depends on the material.
dismantle: Check that it doesn't seal a pressurized room.
Cut it free with the {tools}.
Send it to the {destination}.

entries.summary: Load-bearing frame.
dismantle: Cut it free with the {tools}.
Send it to the {destination}.
tips: Cutting frame can release large sections at once - watch where they drift.

entries.summary: A cut point holding parts together. Cut it and they come apart.
dismantle: Aim the Stinger at it and hold until it breaks.
If its grade is above your cutter's, look for another way to free the part.
tips: Release the Stinger now and then so it doesn't overheat.

entries.summary: A clamp holding parts together. Cut it to release them.
dismantle: Cut it with the Stinger.

entries.summary: Cut Guard foam protects whatever is underneath from being cut.
dismantle: Break it first - it shatters on impact or from a charged Grapple push.
Then cut the part underneath.

entries.summary: Storage. Often heavy.
dismantle: Cut it from its mounts.
Use Tethers for heavy ones - they pull harder than the Grapple and can be stacked.
Send it to the {destination}.

entries.summary: Holds a fuel pod. It cannot be taken apart in the Bay.
dismantle: Don't try to take it apart - cut it free in one piece.
Send it to the {destination}.

entries.summary: Radiation Containment Unit. It houses a fragile, radioactive filter.
dismantle: Remove its access panel to reach the Radiation Filter.
Take the filter out gently and get it to the Barge.
Then cut the unit free and send it to the {destination}.

entries.summary: Access panel covering a Radiation Filter.
dismantle: Remove it to reach the filter behind it.
Send it to the {destination}.

entries.summary: A Space Truck part. Handle it carefully and bring it back in one piece.
Fragile and radioactive.
dismantle: Handle it gently - it breaks easily.
Keep it away from yourself and anything organic.
Deliver it to the {destination}.

warnings: Explosive: cutting, burning or hitting it hard can set it off.
tips: Coolant can neutralize an explosive object.

warnings: Flammable: fire spreads quickly between flammable objects.
Cutting into it starts a leak.
Can arc when removed, hit or damaged, briefly electrifying nearby metal.
tips: The Scanner's Systems Mode shows wires, junction boxes and power sources.

warnings: Radiation hurts you and damages organic material.
A violent decompression flings loose objects toward the breach.
tips: The Scanner shows which rooms are still pressurized.
Frozen objects are brittle - a hard hit can shatter them.

entries.summary: Furniture. Usually harmless - cut it from its mounts.
Ship structure.
Cargo or storage. Often heavy - Tethers help.
Part of the ship's electrical system.
Part of the propulsion system. Expect fuel nearby.
Part of the Environmental Control Unit.
A consumable or collectible. Grab it by hand.
